# Condition-file schema {.unnumbered #condition-file-schema}

## Public interface {#condition-schema-public-interface}

Saved condition files are versioned public interfaces. A file contains application identification, a format name, a schema version, a timestamp, and a `conditions` object containing every persistent user setting for that page.

The ACC Magnetometer currently writes schema **6.10**, including the active
physics-model identifier. Light shift and Atomic polarizability use their own
independently versioned formats.

## Loading {#condition-loading}

The loader validates application and format identifiers before applying values. A complete current-schema file must contain the required fields. Supported older versions pass through explicit migration steps before their settings enter session state.

## Compatibility principles {#condition-compatibility-principles}

- A migrated field must preserve its former physical meaning.
- New defaults must not overwrite values loaded from a file.
- Renaming a page or navigation route does not by itself require a schema change.
- Changing the meaning, units, or structure of a stored field does require a new schema and migration.
- Unknown future schema versions are rejected rather than guessed.

## Probe-source migration {#probe-source-migration}

Schema 6.9 distinguishes explicit weak sources (`PumpN weak`) from physical
pump sources (`PumpN`). Migration from 6.9 preserves those selections and all
other saved inputs, adding `rf_manifold_A/B=Fa`, `probe_manifold_A/B=Total`,
and `probe_show_manifold_decomposition_A/B=false`. New sessions instead use
`rf_manifold_A/B=Both`. Current files require all six new fields; invalid
manifold selections and incomplete older files are rejected before state is
changed. Versions older than 6.9 remain unsupported.

This is a settings migration, not a legacy solver selection. The two-manifold
physics is always active and previous predictions may change.

User workflow is described in [Condition files](../user-manual/condition-files.qmd).
